parameters.note: Lake Aloha is a large, shallow high-alpine reservoir (~8,100 ft) in the Desolation Wilderness (El Dorado Co.), impounded at the head of Desolation Valley. It lies on the western slope of the Sierra crest: its outlet is Pyramid Creek, which drains south to the South Fork American River (Sacramento / American River basin) — outside the Lake Tahoe basin entirely — so the special Lake Tahoe tributary closure (§7.50(b)(152), which reaches only flowing tributaries upstream to the first lake) does not apply. The reservoir is not listed by name in §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so it falls under the general statewide lake regulation §5.85(a)(1): open all year, 5/10. It is not in CDFW's 2026 provisional stocking plan; brook trout and rainbow trout ('Brookies and Rainbows') are reported by a third-party angling reference (flyfishingthesierra.com).

candidates.summary: Open all year (general statewide lake regulation; not listed as a special-regulation water)
